extracted.intended_audience: exchange members, trading permit holders, market participants, and interested SEC commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Notice of a self-regulatory organization (SRO) proposed rule change to amend fee schedules (connectivity fees and/or historical Open-Close Data discounts), including the statutorily required statements justifying the change and solicitation of public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with the Securities Exchange Act (Section 6(b) / 6(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”) and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange, and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act. Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, ... to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filings should explain how the proposed rule change furthers the Act's objectives (prevent fraud/manipulation, promote just and equitable principles, remove impediments to a free and open market, protect investors/public interest) and affirm that the rule is not designed to permit unfair discrimination. Reference to the specific statutory provisions cited (Section 6(b), especially 6(b)(5)) is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: No unnecessary or inappropriate burden on competition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filings should analyze both intramarket and intermarket competition: explain whether the change applies uniformly to similarly situated participants, whether it could create barriers to entry (e.g., for smaller participants), and whether alternatives exist (such as lower-cost options or third-party resellers). Use market context and objective measures to support the conclusion that any burden is necessary and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness, equity, and absence of unfair discrimination in pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange believes the proposed monthly per port fee (or data fee/discount) is reasonable, equitable and not unfairly discriminatory since it would be assessed uniformly across all market participants that purchase the physical ports (or historical data) and, where applicable, the Exchange will not charge multiple fees for the same port.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the fee will be applied uniformly (which participants it applies to), whether the fee differentiates among participants and why (if it does), and any mechanisms to avoid double-charging (e.g., single-port fee across affiliate exchanges). Show that similarly situated participants are treated the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of fees based on value and resource consumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange believes increasing the fee for 10 Gb physical ports and charging a higher fee as compared to the 1 Gb physical port is equitable as the 1 Gb physical port is of lower value and does not offer access to many products/services; market participants that purchase 10 Gb physical ports utilize the most bandwidth and therefore consume the most resources from the network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide factual support (statistics on port distribution/usage, anticipated demand by data center, resource consumption rationale) demonstrating that differentiated pricing reflects the relative value and resource consumption of the services (e.g., 10Gb vs 1Gb).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of objective, stable metrics to adjust fees (e.g., Data Processing PPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange evaluated its proposed fee change using an objective and stable metric with limited volatility. Utilizing Data Processing PPI over a specified period of time is a reasonable means of recouping a portion of the Exchange's investment in maintaining and enhancing the connectivity service identified above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing inflation- or index-based fee adjustments, identify the chosen metric, justify its suitability (tailored measure, limited volatility), describe the period used, and explain how it maps to the costs the Exchange seeks to recoup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of detailed product description and voluntary nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing describes products (End-of-Day and Intraday Open-Close Data), noting that EOD is an end-of-day volume summary at the option level by origin/side/price/transaction type and Intraday provides snapshots every 10 minutes; these data products are proprietary, historical (not real-time), voluntary, and available on a subscription or ad-hoc basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise product descriptions (content, frequency/update timing, proprietary scope), distribution methods (subscription/ad-hoc), whether product is voluntary or required, and how it competes with substitute products offered by other exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of competitive substitutes and market context
rubrics_metrics.description: Open-Close Data is subject to direct competition from similar end-of-day and intraday options trading summaries offered by several other options exchanges (e.g., Nasdaq PHLX Options Trade Outline, ISE Profile, GEMX Trade Profile, open-close data from other exchanges). The market is highly competitive (e.g., 18 registered options exchanges; no single exchange >17% market share).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List competing products/exchanges and provide relevant market-share or market-structure context to support claims about competitive constraints on pricing (to show why the fee is not supracompetitive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of incentive/discount program terms and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange proposes a temporary 20% discount on ad-hoc purchases of historical Open-Close Data for any single purchase of $20,000 or more, effective April 23, 2025 through June 30, 2025; the discount applies order-by-order, will not aggregate purchases across a billing cycle, cannot be combined with other discounts (including academic discounts), and applies equally to Trading Permit Holders and non-Trading Permit Holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit program parameters: discount percentage, qualifying threshold, effective dates, scope of applicability (which customers), whether orders are aggregated, combinability with other discounts, and an example calculation (e.g., $25,000 order discounted to $20,000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of fee change as promoting use/competition/innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange believes the proposed discount will give purchasers the ability to use and test the historical Open-Close Data at a discounted rate, encourage purchases, broaden availability of market data, and, more generally, promote competition and innovation consistent with Regulation NMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the fee change/incentive will further public interest goals (e.g., broaden data availability, enable testing/use, drive competition among data providers) and reference relevant regulatory principles (e.g., Regulation NMS preference for market competition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of actual investments and ongoing costs where fee increases are proposed
rubrics_metrics.description: To support connectivity fee changes the Exchange documents investments and costs (multi-year initiative to improve platform performance and capacity; switch hardware upgrades increasing determinism and port capacity by nearly 50%; nearly two-fold network bandwidth increase; costs to prepare and maintain NY6 data center including power/space/fiber/cabinets/panels/labor/maintenance; costs to latency-equalize NY6; portal updates; weekly proactive audits). The Exchange notes these costs were incurred and not otherwise passed through or offset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing fee increases tied to infrastructure, enumerate specific capital expenditures and ongoing operating costs, explain how they improve service (performance, capacity, determinism, latency equalization), and state whether those costs have been or will be recovered previously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration that pricing will not create barriers to smaller participants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange says the proposed connectivity pricing is associated with relative usage; market participants with modest capacity needs can continue to buy the less expensive 1 Gb physical port (unchanged) or obtain access via a third-party re-seller. Accordingly, the proposed connectivity fees do not favor certain categories of market participants in a manner that would impose a burden on competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain alternatives available to smaller participants, show that lower-cost options remain (or third-party resellers exist), and demonstrate that the allocation reflects network resource consumption so as not to unfairly exclude smaller firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing availability, inspection, and public disclosure practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website, at the Exchange's Office of the Secretary, and at the Commission's Public Reference Room. The Commission will post all comments on its internet website. Copies of the submission and related communications will be available for inspection and copying, except materials withheld under 5 U.S.C. 552 (and obscene or copyright-protected material may be redacted or withheld).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide locations/URLs where the filing and its exhibits may be examined, state how the Commission will publish comments, and include any redaction/withholding policies (PII instructions, obscene/copyright exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation procedures and comment instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the proposal by: (1) using the Commission’s internet comment form; or (2) sending an email to rule-comments@sec.gov (include file number SR-... on subject line). Paper comments may be sent in triplicate to the SEC Secretary. All submissions should refer to the file number and be submitted by the stated deadline (e.g., on or before June 12, 2025). Do not include personally identifiable information; submit only information you wish to make public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear instructions for electronic and paper submission, the required file number to include, deadlines, and guidance on not submitting PII and how submissions will be handled/published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of effectiveness and Commission summary suspension timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and paragraph (f) of Rule 19b-4. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act; if it takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine approval or disapproval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the statutory authority for immediate effectiveness (where applicable) and explain the Commission's 60-day summary suspension authority and follow-on proceeding process so commenters understand the procedural timeline.
